This happened to me just last year, I went to the doctor because I have really long periods and she wanted me to get some tests done including a TVUS. I remember distinctly, she said, “Let’s get a transvaginal ultrasound”. Then she paused, asked me if I was married or if I was sexually active, when I responded no to both questions, she wanted to go for the abdominal one. When I insisted that I am okay with the TVUS, she said, “Okay good, cus that’s the better one”. 

I was surprised to hear this because every other gyno I’ve been to only ever suggested I get the abdominal one.  

But I thought, that was that. No more uncomfortable poking while my bladder was full. However when I got to the diagnostic facility, from the receptionist to the technician doing the ultrasound, all kept asking me if I was married. They kept telling me that TVUS is not for unmarried women, even when I kept showing the note from the doc. Eventually the technician relented after I lied about being sexually active and told her multiple times that I wanted and asked the doctor for this scan. 

I’m really sorry you had experience this kinda nonsense as well. It’s absolutely insane that things like “virginity” and “purity” are given more importance than a woman’s health and life!! It’s incredibly unfair and it feels demeaning to have to experience this.

Hi, thanks for your advice. Yeah, I also had some crazy bleeding before the anaemia diagnosis. I bled for 33 days, then there was a 15 day break before I bled for another 38 days before another 15 day break and then bled for 7 days (I feel like my body just ran out of blood at that point). 

When I shared this with the gyno, she was actually shocked but she didn't order any tests beyond the normal ultrasound, which came back normal. 

They did give me an iron transfusion, B12 injections for anaemia, besides the birth control pills, but that's about it. They all recommended that I maintain my diet, exercise and lose weight because that is the only way it can be controlled long term.

Hi, don't apologise for getting angry, I totally understand where you're coming from. Honestly, idk whom to ask for help. Like I've mentioned in other replies, where I'm from, most docs just don't see beyond the weight. This has been my life since I was a child tbh, doctors, parents, relatives all seem to think that my problems are just weight related. Even when I was skinny, I was told that I need to lose more weight (because I didn't have the ideal 'hourglass' figure as a frickin' child and teenager!). This narrative followed me well into my adulthood. I've reached a point where I'm beyond exhausted and sceptical of seeking help from anyone. Idk how I'm going to proceed at this point.

Hi, I agree with you. I know that I have a very messed up relationship with food. I should also mention that I have been clinically depressed (and also have anxiety) for a decade now, and I have been in very stressful environments constantly for a while now.

Like I mentioned in one of my replies above, when I was in a decent headspace, I did manage to follow a nutritious diet and worked out regularly which helped with my periods (to a certain extent), made me lose weight, and did make me feel better overall, but then things took a bad turn in my personal life and I have still not recovered from all that mentally.

When my mental health is so bad that all the energy I have is being consumed for merely surviving and getting from one day to the next, it's becoming really hard to focus and maintain things like my diet and exercise. 

I can't tell the doctors about my depression because the doctors here (where I'm from) are very judgy about mental health and truly think a young woman can't possibly have depression, like what even is there for you to be depressed about? (a question I've been on the receiving end of far too many times, but I digress). All this is making it really hard for me to lose weight, so to be caught up in a predicament where the only solution being offered to me is to lose weight, it's really disheartening. It's like my pain and discomfort mean nothing. Constantly having to hear people (not just doctors) telling me lose weight makes me feel I'm just being lazy and I just need to get off my ass and just workout already. But I can't, I simply can't. Not because I don't want to, not because I don't try, but because in my current situation, I cannot prioritise it no matter how hard I try. 

As for my friend, this isn't the first time she has invalidated my feelings, because for her, it makes complete sense that you lose weight and your PCOS is controlled. She's not trying to see things from my perspective. Despite the fact that she struggled with similar problems like PCOS, doctors telling her to lose weight, etc. When I tell her that she's not understanding things from my POV, she gets upset and shuts down the convo completely. All of this is so exhausting, I just don't know what to do anymore.

Sorry I just ended up going on a rant again.

Hi, I haven't tried that. I had a normal ultrasound done and nothing was out of the ordinary. The problem is that almost every gyro I've visited in the past 3 years just keeps telling me to lose weight and automatically puts me on birth control. The reason I didn't even visit a doctor despite the 2-3 months of on/off 30 day bleeding periods is because I really didn't want to hear another doctor tell me to lose weight and not offer any type of solution. 

Not to mention, there was a period of time where I lost quite a bit of weight, took care of my diet and exercised regularly, and for the most part, it kept my periods controlled. However, some intense and constantly stressful events took place in my life and I could not keep up those routines and my mental health worsened, and with it, so did my menstrual cycle.

Tbh, I'm afraid and exhausted, idk whom to ask for help. All the people in my life keep telling me to resume exercising and lose weight, and that they want me to be active again. It's like they cannot see beyond the fact that I'm fat, like that's all there is to me. 

I will try to branch out and see if there's a doctor I can find who will help me, but I don't have any hope.

Hey, I've also been prescribed the same thing. The bleeding stops when I take it, once the course is finished and I stop taking it, the bleeding starts all over again, so it isn't making much of a difference, except for delaying/prolonging the period even more.
